expectations.text: A: Recognizes this is the same root cause as eval 2 (each-hydrate deferral) — not a snippet-specific bug
expectations.evidence: The answer focuses primarily on demonstrating that the canonical case works (passing test at line 1408) and explores the mechanism in detail. It explains the each-content-classifier bails on snippets forcing the eager path, but does NOT explicitly tie this back to eval 2's root cause (each-hydrate deferral as the underlying mechanism). It frames the discussion around 'the framework path works for the canonical shape' rather than 'this is the same lazy-hydrate deferral pattern that was at risk.'

expectations.text: B: Explains that snippet args (`label=item.name`) are evaluated by the per-item content path; the snippet body sees those args via `buildSnippetProxy`
expectations.evidence: Section 3 ('The snippet block on the hydrate path') explicitly explains: 'When `template.hydrate` runs with `data = itemProxy` (the each-item proxy) and `kind === 'snippet'`, it calls `buildSnippetProxy(node, itemProxy, evaluator)` to build the snippet-args overlay.' It then quotes the lazy getter code from template.js:67-114 showing how arg getters close over the each-item proxy and walk through itemProxy.get('item') to subscribe to itemSignal.value.

expectations.text: C: Notes that without per-item Reactions wired, the snippet arg evaluation never re-runs when items change in place
expectations.evidence: The answer explains the chain in section 4 'The mutation path': itemSignal.notify() wakes everything subscribed to that per-item signal, including the snippet body's text Reaction. By describing the mechanism that makes it work (per-item Reactions getting wired via adoptServerItems on the eager path), it implicitly establishes that without those wired Reactions the snippet args wouldn't re-evaluate. Case A in 'Why your case might not be doing this' explicitly addresses 'no reconcile, no snapshot diff, no per-item notify.'

expectations.text: D: Identifies that the each-content-classifier conservatively bails on snippet/template/rerender/async invocations (treating them as cross-AST/dynamic) — forcing eager adoption — which is the fix
expectations.evidence: Section 1 ('The self-contained classifier bails on snippet calls') quotes the exact code from each-content-classifier.js line 189: 'case 'template': case 'snippet': case 'rerender': case 'guard': case 'async': return false;' and explains: 'snippet bodies live in a separate AST, and the classifier doesn't trace cross-AST identifier flow. Rather than guess wrong it bails conservative — meaning your each gets the *eager* wire path.'
